school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented LSU rituals, honors, songs, objects, and game-day practices drawn from current university and athletics sources.

cards.title: Meet the Living Face of LSU
cards.subtitle: LSU’s live-tiger mascot tradition
cards.notes: Visit Mike’s campus habitat respectfully, follow posted guidance, and use LSU’s history page to identify each tiger in the lineage.
cards.short_summary: A student-funded idea became an enduring live-mascot program represented today by Mike VII.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that Mike VII arrived on campus on August 15, 2017, and continues a live-mascot program established more than 85 years ago.
cards.source_title: About LSU: What Is LSU Known For? And Other LSU Facts
cards.access_notes: Observe Mike only from public visitor areas and follow all habitat rules; animal appearances are not guaranteed.

cards.title: Line the Route on Victory Hill
cards.subtitle: The team-and-band procession before LSU home football games
cards.notes: Check the official game-day schedule, then stand along the designated public route early enough to watch the team and Tiger Band pass.
cards.short_summary: Players, musicians, and generations of spectators converge on one ceremonial approach to Tiger Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU reports that before every home game, fans line the street while the Golden Band from Tigerland parades the football team down Victory Hill and plays the Pregame Salute.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: This occurs on LSU home-football game days; consult the current official event schedule and observe route controls.

cards.title: Answer the First Four Notes
cards.subtitle: Tiger Band’s ceremonial Tiger Stadium entrance
cards.notes: Be in position before kickoff and listen for the opening four notes; join the crowd’s LSU response without blocking aisles or entrances.
cards.short_summary: Four notes from the Golden Band cue a stadium-wide response before the Tigers take the field.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes its pregame show as a tradition in which the opening four notes of the Pregame Salute prompt the crowd to chant “LSU” as the band lines up.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: Presented inside Tiger Stadium before football games; stadium entry requires the applicable event credential.

cards.title: Stay for the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: The student section’s ritual after a Tiger Stadium win
cards.notes: After a home victory, remain through the band’s alma mater and follow the student section’s lead while stadium departure begins around you.
cards.short_summary: A win closes with students swaying together as the band plays LSU’s alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU documents that after every Tiger Stadium victory, the student section sways and sings while the band plays the LSU Alma Mater.
cards.source_title: Saturday Night in Death Valley: An LSU Game Day Through Students’ Eyes
cards.access_notes: This contingent postgame ritual occurs inside Tiger Stadium after LSU victories; event admission is required.

cards.title: Clap Along Before Kickoff
cards.subtitle: Tiger Stadium’s recorded pregame singalong
cards.notes: Listen just before kickoff for the opening notes, then clap or sing from your seat while keeping stairs and stadium circulation paths clear.
cards.short_summary: A Garth Brooks recording turns the minutes before kickoff into a coordinated LSU crowd ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics states that every home game, immediately before kickoff in Tiger Stadium, “Callin’ Baton Rouge” plays and fans stand, clap, and sing along.
cards.access_notes: Occurs inside Tiger Stadium at LSU home football games; event admission is required.

cards.title: Spell Out Tigers After the Score
cards.subtitle: The band-and-crowd response to an LSU touchdown
cards.notes: After an LSU touchdown, listen for Tiger Band’s motif and join the spelled-out response from your seat without entering restricted areas.
cards.short_summary: A short band cue converts each LSU touchdown into a collective spelling lesson.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics documents that after a Tigers touchdown, the band plays the “Tiger Rag” motif and fans respond by spelling out “T-I-G-E-R-S.”
cards.access_notes: This score-triggered ritual occurs inside Tiger Stadium during football games; event admission is required.

cards.title: Look for White on the Home Side
cards.subtitle: LSU football’s inverted home-uniform convention
cards.notes: At a home game, photograph the team’s white jerseys from your assigned area and compare the combination with LSU’s documented uniform history.
cards.short_summary: LSU’s home team often wears the color normally associated with visiting football teams.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Athletics traces its home-white-jersey tradition to the 1958 national-championship season and says the practice returned in 1995 after a rules change.
cards.source_title: Football to Wear Traditional White Jerseys in BCS Game
cards.access_notes: Uniform combinations vary by game; verify the current matchup through LSU Athletics before relying on this tradition.

cards.title: Spot the Double-Post Silhouette
cards.subtitle: A preserved LSU football-field tradition
cards.notes: From an authorized stadium seat or broadcast view, compare the double-support goalpost shape with the conventional single-post design.
cards.short_summary: Tiger Stadium preserves an old-fashioned goalpost profile as a deliberate piece of LSU football identity.
cards.evidence_claim: An official LSU Athletics letter identifies the H-style goalposts among LSU football’s time-honored traditions.
cards.source_title: A Letter From Joe Alleva - July 2016
cards.access_notes: View from authorized stadium areas during an event or tour; never enter the playing field without permission.

cards.title: Let Mike Watch Over the Rings
cards.subtitle: The LSU Ring’s pre-ceremony overnight ritual
cards.notes: Order by the published deadline if eligible, then follow Student Affairs instructions so your ring can join the overnight habitat tradition.
cards.short_summary: Eligible LSU rings spend a ceremonial night under Mike’s watch before their owners receive them.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Student Affairs states that rings ordered by its stated deadline may participate in Overnight with Mike, when Mike watches over the rings in his habitat overnight.
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited by LSU Ring eligibility, purchase, ordering deadlines, and current ceremony instructions.

cards.title: Recognize Twelve Graduating Tigers
cards.subtitle: LSU’s annual senior honor built around scholarship, leadership, and service
cards.notes: Read the current eligibility rules, nominate an eligible senior by the posted deadline, or follow LSU’s announcement of the new class.
cards.short_summary: Each spring, LSU distills a graduating class into twelve examples of campus and community contribution.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Student Affairs states that each spring it recognizes 12 outstanding seniors who contribute positively to campus, the surrounding community, or society.
cards.access_notes: Applications and nominations are limited to published eligibility windows; viewing the recipient page is public.
